param.name: reference_source_selector
param.label: Choose the source for the reference genome file
param.option: Use a genome from the history

param.name: region_type
param.label: Regions to call
param.help: VarDict holds per-position data for the whole region being processed in memory, so restricting to your actual targets (a BED or defined regions) keeps memory low. Calling entire chromosomes is expensive.
param.option: A BED file of target regions (recommended)

param.name: bed_file
param.label: Target regions BED
param.help: Tab-separated chr, start, end (0-based, as standard BED). A 4th name/gene column is used if present, otherwise the chromosome name is used. Only these regions are processed, keeping memory low.

param.name: regions_text
param.label: Target regions
param.help: One region per line, BED-style and whitespace-separated: chr start end [name] (0-based start). Example: chr1 1647000 1648500. Only these regions are processed.

param.name: region
param.label: Region of interest (-R)
param.help: A single region, 1-based, format chr:start-end (e.g. chr1:1647000-1648500). WARNING: this processes the ENTIRE region as one unit and holds all of its per-position data in memory at once, so passing a whole chromosome here can use a very large amount of RAM. For anything larger than a locus, prefer a BED file or typed regions.

param.name: interval_file
param.label: Chromosomes
param.help: Optional: restrict to this list of chromosomes (one per line). WARNING: calling across whole chromosomes is memory-intensive; prefer a target BED where possible.
